question: A patient on daily insulin glargine injection reports that her fasting glucose has become increasingly erratic over the past 3 months, despite no diet or medication changes. On examination, you notice a soft, painless, fatty lump at her usual injection site. What is the most likely cause and correct management?

answers.text: Insulin resistance has developed — switch to a higher dose insulin

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The painless fatty lump at the injection site is lipohypertrophy — a result of repeatedly injecting into the same spot. This impairs insulin absorption, causing erratic glucose. The solution is site rotation, not a dose increase.

answers.text: Lipohypertrophy from injection site non-rotation — counsel on site rotation and avoid the affected area

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Lipohypertrophy develops when the same subcutaneous site is used repeatedly. Insulin absorption from fibrotic/fatty tissue is unpredictable. Management: rotate within and across sites (abdomen, thighs, arms, buttocks) and avoid the lipohypertrophied area until it resolves.

answers.text: Lipoatrophy from immune reaction to human insulin — switch to insulin analogue

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Lipoatrophy (depression/indentation) is a different finding caused by immune reaction. This case describes lipohypertrophy (lump), which is caused by mechanical trauma from repeated injection, not immune reaction.

answers.text: Subcutaneous infection at the injection site — prescribe antibiotics

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A subcutaneous infection would be tender, erythematous, and warm. A painless, soft, fatty lump over weeks is the classic description of lipohypertrophy.

overallFeedback.feedback: Lipohypertrophy is painless (often missed), caused by repeated trauma to the same site. It impairs insulin absorption and causes unpredictable glucose. Treatment: site rotation and avoiding the affected area.
Well done — lipohypertrophy from poor site rotation is a common, preventable cause of erratic insulin absorption. Always examine injection sites.
